samples.summary: The "reached by alias" test never goes through an alias — it is tautological
samples.evidence: `it('reports the canonical name when the command was reached by alias')` builds `program.command('docs').alias('doc')` and then calls `outputError(new Error('boom'), docs.command('content'))` directly. No argv is ever parsed, so the command is not "reached by alias" in any sense; the test passes the canonical `Command` object itself. `commandPath` (src/output/formatter.ts:58-64) reads `c.name()`, which in commander always returns the canonical name and never the alias, so this assertion is true regardless of whether alias handling works — including if `.alias('doc')` were deleted entirely. The behavior it claims to guard (running `wafflebase doc content …` and getting `command:"docs.content"` in the envelope) would require `parseAsync(['node','wafflebase','doc','content'])` and inspecting the emitted envelope; no such test exists in this file.

samples.summary: The one non-catch `outputError(..., this)` call site (tabs create, unsupported --type) has no assertion on `command`
samples.evidence: tabs.ts:35-38 is the only added call site outside a `catch`, i.e. a distinct code path. packages/cli/test/tabs.test.ts:108-111 parses the envelope but only asserts `err.error.message` matches /only "sheet" is supported/; nothing asserts `error.command === 'sheets.tabs.create'`, so dropping or mis-passing `this` there is invisible. Searched: grep for `error\.command|command:` across packages/cli/test (only output.test.ts hits) and read tabs.test.ts.

samples.summary: ~40 changed call sites, only two asserted: notes/slides/files/api-keys/sheets-export/import envelopes are never checked for `command`
samples.evidence: The diff threads `this` into outputError at every command in api-keys.ts, cells.ts, docs.ts, files.ts, notes.ts, sheets-export.ts, sheets-import.ts, slides.ts and tabs.ts. Tests only assert `command` for `docs.get` (output.test.ts:343-347) and `sheets.cells.get` (output.test.ts:352-359). The other suites (docs-import, notes-import, slides-import, files-upload, files-download) parse the same envelope but assert only `code`/`message`, so a missed or wrong `this` in those files would ship silently. This is coverage breadth, not a missing core behavior, hence minor.

samples.summary: The single-line invariant is only tested with newline-free messages
samples.evidence: `getEmittedBody` asserts `expect(raw).not.toContain('\n')` but every error fed to it ('boom', 'bad zip', 'HTTP 500', 'plain string failure') is already newline-free, so the assertion holds even for the old pretty-printed form? — no, pretty-printing would add newlines, so it does catch that. What it does not cover is the interesting case for a line-delimited stderr parser: an error whose *message* contains a literal newline (JSON.stringify escapes it, but nothing pins that). No test in packages/cli/test constructs such an error.

samples.summary: The `preAction` attribution path is only tested for a top-level command, not a nested one
samples.evidence: The runCli test (output.test.ts:421-438) registers `program.command('boom')` and asserts `command:'boom'`, a single-segment path where `commandPath` does almost nothing. The doc comment claims attribution matters most on this path; a nested unhandled rejection (e.g. `sheets cells get` throwing outside its try) is never driven through runCli, so a hook that captured `_thisCommand` instead of `actionCommand` would still pass. Searched output.test.ts and cli-related tests for other runCli invocations.

samples.summary: The doc claim that commandPath yields the same string the schema registry indexes on is untested
samples.evidence: formatter.ts:51-57 asserts the dotted path equals what `schema` indexes on, but no test cross-checks real registered command paths against `getAllCommandSchemas()` names. schema.test.ts:128-146 checks registry names in isolation; output.test.ts checks commandPath in isolation. Drift between the two (a renamed subcommand) would break the documented contract with no failing test.

finding.summary: The "reached by alias" test never goes through an alias — it is tautological
finding.evidence: `it('reports the canonical name when the command was reached by alias')` builds `program.command('docs').alias('doc')` and then calls `outputError(new Error('boom'), docs.command('content'))` directly. No argv is ever parsed, so the command is not "reached by alias" in any sense; the test passes the canonical `Command` object itself. `commandPath` (src/output/formatter.ts:58-64) reads `c.name()`, which in commander always returns the canonical name and never the alias, so this assertion is true regardless of whether alias handling works — including if `.alias('doc')` were deleted entirely. verdict.reason: The test exists verbatim as described at packages/cli/test/output.test.ts:197-202. It never parses argv: it constructs `program.command('docs').alias('doc')` and passes the canonical subcommand object `docs.command('content')` directly to `outputError`. The code under test, `commandPath` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:58-64), walks `c.parent` and reads `c.name()`, and `outputError` (formatter.ts:80-93) reads nothing else — neither touches `aliases()` or any invoked-name resolution. Therefore the assertion `'docs.content'` is true regardless of whether alias handling works, and remains green if `.alias('doc')` is deleted; it is a duplicate of the nested-command test at lines 190-195. The behavior the test title claims to guard (running through the `doc` alias and getting `command:"docs.content"` in the envelope, as documented in formatter.ts:52-56) is not covered anywhere: the parseAsync-driven envelope tests in the same file (lines 304-375, helper `run()` at 304-306) only use canonical names such as `docs get` and `sheets cells get`; namespaces.test.ts:36-67 only asserts `aliases()` array contents without executing a command; schema.test.ts:168 covers schema-registry alias strings, not the error envelope. No refutation ground applies — the code is present as described, no guard makes it moot, and a vacuous test presented as coverage of a stated behavior is exactly this lens's lane.

finding.summary: Alias test is vacuous — it never reaches the command by alias
finding.evidence: `it('reports the canonical name when the command was reached by alias')` builds `program.command('docs').alias('doc')` and then calls `outputError(new Error('boom'), docs.command('content'))` directly. No parsing happens, so the command is never "reached by alias" at all; the assertion `command === 'docs.content'` holds purely because `commandPath` walks `name()` on objects the test itself constructed. Deleting `.alias('doc')` leaves the test green, so it provides zero coverage for the alias-collapsing behavior the doc comment in formatter.ts:53-56 claims (`wafflebase doc content` still reports `docs.content`). A real guard would drive `parseAsync(['node','wafflebase','doc','content', ...])` through the registered program with a failing fetch and assert the envelope's `command`.

verdict.reason: Verified the test exists exactly as quoted. output.test.ts:197-202 calls outputError() directly on a Command object it constructed; no parse/parseAsync runs, so the command is never actually reached via the alias. commandPath (formatter.ts:58-64) walks c.name(), which returns 'docs' whether or not .alias('doc') was ever called, so removing the alias call leaves the assertion green — the test is a duplicate of the nested-path test at output.test.ts:190-195 and gives zero coverage for the alias-collapsing behavior documented at formatter.ts:50-57. I searched for any alternative guard: namespaces.test.ts:36-67 only asserts aliases() membership (never emits an envelope or calls commandPath); schema.test.ts:168-199 tests getCommandSchema's separate string alias table, not commandPath; and the parseAsync-driven envelope tests (output.test.ts:333-359) only drive canonical names (docs get, sheets cells get), never a real alias such as 'doc' (docs.ts:61-63) or 'cell' (cells.ts:9). Fake coverage for a named behavior with no other test covering it is major under the test-adequacy rubric.
